title: omg what's happening
speaker: Kevin Paffrath (Meet Kevin)

macro_themes.view: Oil-driven price pass-through and resilient high-income spending force the Fed's hand toward hikes.

macro_themes.theme: Iran deal as the key catalyst
macro_themes.view: Expects an Iran deal around Oct 20-27; until then expect volatility, after it oil and yields fall.
10y respected the 5.27% ceiling and is falling while the 2y holds, signalling growth fears; TLT bottoming.
CoreWeave's debt is distressed and neoclouds will likely be absorbed by hyperscalers, weighing on hardware.
Gold peaks 3-5 years after QE; under a no-printing Warsh Fed gold is in a lost period, next peak ~2033-2035.
AI is cutting hiring outside specialised trades, which is deflationary longer term and may temper Fed hikes.

calls.condition: Would get excited buying the dip only if QQQ drops to 712-700; recovery expected after an Iran deal
calls.reason: QQQ lost the 735 line; expects volatility and buy-the-dip opportunities until an Iran deal, which he expects Oct 20-27.
calls.quote: you got to bring me back to like 712 or 700 on the Nasdaq 100 and then I'll get excited about buying the dip

calls.reason: 10y respected the 5.27 peak and gave back all of CPI-day gains; growth fears bring bids, and an Iran deal would push yields down.
calls.quote: I still maintain 527 is the ceiling.

calls.condition: Bigger upside on an Iran deal
calls.reason: TLT recaptured the 77-78 line it keeps bouncing off on the weekly; hardware fears turning into Treasury buying.
calls.quote: the more people get nervous about hardware, the more TLT actually confirms its bottom

calls.condition: Bearish until Warsh turns on the money printer or is replaced (~May 2030); next gold peak 2033-2035 if printing resumes
calls.reason: Gold peaks 3-5 years after QE; a no-printing Warsh regime plus a clear momentum downtrend and an Iran deal lifting bonds keeps gold weak.
calls.quote: when you combine Warsh with timing of money printer and momentum, you have a bearish outlook

calls.reason: Memory is a commoditised product; 2026 is the memory peak with new US supply and Chinese state-backed DRAM competition.
calls.quote: I'm bearish memory and the memory cycle. I'm also bearish uh SanDisk

calls.reason: Higher-cost US supply plus cheaper Chinese DRAM is a double-edged hit to Micron as memory peaks.
calls.quote: You kind of got a double-edged hit there on a on a memory play like a Micron

calls.condition: Hardware weak until an Iran deal and memory fears pass, then recovers
calls.reason: Higher yields and neocloud stress hit hardware now; cheaper memory later benefits logic makers like Nvidia; prefers buying semis over gold.
calls.quote: I'm actually bullish a hardware recovery once we get through the Iran situation

calls.reason: Green on a red day; the exception to bearish hardware because it doesn't spend on data centers, and it pockets cheaper memory in margins.
calls.quote: you have to be bearish hardware with the exception of Apple

calls.reason: Balance sheet is horrible, ~$8B short, bonds at distressed levels; likely bankruptcy or absorption by hyperscalers.
calls.quote: Can it go bankrupt? Of course. Yeah. Uh they their balance sheet is horrible.

calls.reason: Thinks Netflix will be a huge beneficiary of AI efficiencies after laying off ~1,000 workers.
calls.quote: You know what I actually think is going to be a huge beneficiary of investing in artificial intelligence? Netflix.

notes: Date inferred from host: CPI 'this morning', Warsh speaks 'Thursday. That's tomorrow' -> Wednesday 2026-10-14 (listing said 10-15). QQQ price = 725.50 line + 0.89 as he described. 10y price not given exactly ('still under 5.2'). Gold Kalshi discussion: he leans to 'No' on gold >= $4,500 by year end and notes 57% odds of gold < $4,300; not recorded as targets. Fed odds: ~35% October hike, December hike near certain.
